title: Hiring Bicycles for a Day Out

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: Good morning, Harbourside Cycle Hire, Joanne speaking. How can I help you?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Oh, hi there. I'm ringing because my family and I are coming to stay in the area next week, and we'd like to hire some bikes for a day. Could I make a booking?

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: Of course, I can sort that out for you now. Can I take your name first?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Yeah, it's Tom Fenwick.

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: Is that F-E-N-N...?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: No, just the one N. F-E-N-W-I-C-K.

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: Lovely, thank you. And where will you be staying while you're here?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: We've rented a cottage. The address is 14 Marlow Street. That's M-A-R-L-O-W.

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: And which day were you thinking of?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: We arrive on the twenty-first, so I was going to say the twenty-second, the Saturday... actually, hang on, my wife's just reminded me we've got a boat trip booked that day. So let's make it the twenty-third, the Sunday.

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: The twenty-third. How many bikes will you need?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Two adults and one child. Our daughter's nine.

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: Okay. For the adults, we have three main types. There are road bikes, which are light and quick but not very comfortable for a whole day; there are mountain bikes; and there are hybrids, which are somewhere in between.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: I was thinking mountain bikes, actually, because I'd heard some of the trails round here are a bit rough.

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: Well, they're good on the forest tracks, but most of our customers stick to the paved paths and the canal, and mountain bikes are quite heavy for that. I'd honestly suggest hybrids. They've got wider tyres than a road bike, so they cope with gravel, but they're much easier to pedal.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Right, that makes sense. Let's go with hybrids, then.

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: Great. And for your daughter we've got a whole range of children's bikes. If you let me know her height when you come in, we'll fit her properly. Helmets and locks are included for everyone, by the way. Do you need anything else?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Oh, good. Is there anything for carrying stuff? We'll want to take a picnic.

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: We can fit a basket on the front of one of the adult bikes, no charge. Some people ask for panniers, the bags that go on the back, but we've stopped hiring those, I'm afraid. Too many came back damaged.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: A basket would be fine.

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: I'll put that down. Now, prices. A full day on a hybrid is eighteen pounds per adult.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Eighteen. Is that the same for the electric bikes? I saw them on your website.

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: No, the electric ones are thirty-two for the day. And a half-day on a hybrid is twelve, but you'd have to bring it back by one o'clock.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: No, I think we want the whole day. And how much for my daughter's bike?

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: Children's bikes are ten pounds a day.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Fine. Do you need a deposit?

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: We don't take a cash deposit, but we do need to see some identification for each adult when you collect the bikes, and we keep a copy. It has to be a passport.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Not a driving licence? That's what I usually carry.

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: I'm afraid not. We used to accept them, but our insurance company changed the rules this year, so it's passports only now.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Okay, I'll make sure we bring them. Now, where do we pick the bikes up? Is it the shop on the harbour front?

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: That's our main shop, yes, but on Sundays it doesn't open until eleven. Most people collect from our kiosk at the railway station instead, which opens at half past eight. Or we can deliver to your cottage, but there's a fifteen-pound charge for that.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Hmm, I don't think we need delivery. The station's only ten minutes' walk from us. We'll get them from there; we want an early start.

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: Good idea. Have you thought about where you'll ride?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: I was looking at the coastal path on the map. It looks beautiful.

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: It is, normally, but part of it's closed for repairs after the storms last month, so you'd have to turn back halfway. Then there's the forest trail, but there's a long, steep climb at the start, which might be hard for a nine-year-old. What I'd recommend is the canal towpath. It's completely flat, there's a lovely café at the lock about eight miles along, and you can usually see herons.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: That sounds perfect for us, actually. We'll do the canal.

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: One last thing. Our closing time on Sundays in summer is half past six, but we ask that all bikes are back at the kiosk by six, so the mechanic has time to check them over.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Six o'clock, got it. Do I need to pay anything now?

script.speaker: Assistant
script.text: No, you pay when you collect. I'll email you a confirmation this afternoon.

groups.instructions: Complete the form below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

questions.explanation: Tom corrects the double N: the name is spelled F-E-N-W-I-C-K.
The cottage is at 14 Marlow Street, which Tom spells out.
He first says the twenty-second but changes it because of a boat trip, so the hire is on Sunday the twenty-third.
Tom considers mountain bikes but accepts the suggestion of hybrids.
Panniers are no longer hired, so a basket is fitted on the front.
A full day on a hybrid costs £18; £32 is for electric bikes and £12 for a half-day.
Driving licences are no longer accepted; only passports.

groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

questions.prompt: Where will Tom's family collect the bikes?

options.text: at the main shop on the harbour front
at the kiosk at the railway station

questions.explanation: The main shop opens late on Sundays and delivery costs extra, so Tom chooses the station kiosk.

questions.prompt: Which route does the assistant recommend?
questions.explanation: The coastal path is partly closed and the forest trail is steep, so she recommends the flat canal towpath.

questions.prompt: By what time must the bikes be returned?
questions.explanation: The kiosk closes at 6.30, but bikes must be back by six so they can be checked.
